      "observations": [
        "All 3,141 owned diff lines across all 68 paths, including every changed test hunk and the deleted 122-line startup service and 46-line startup test, are read. Five cal service properties now resolve lazy module exports; manager, timezone, free/busy, ICS and week-info exports are singleton instances, while ICS property/component types become classes. Interface and component/build removal are checked separately from source moves.",
        "The old ordered startup chain registered localization sources, then initialized timezones, manager and a null-subject completion notification. The manager now side-effect-imports the timezone module, whose constructor patches ICAL and loads timezone/default-pref state before the manager constructor registers its own listeners. The ordered startup API/test and manager/timezone shutdown methods are removed. AlarmService still has a distinct startup/observer lifecycle; this is not a claim that every Calendar service self-starts or needs no cleanup.",
        "A separate Thunderbird window startup producer still emits calendar-startup-done with the window subject, and calWindowUtils still watches that topic when opening a new main window. The selected startup range is disjoint from unrelated product code. Removal of the startup-service producer does not mean the topic disappeared everywhere or that module initialization equals window readiness.",
        "Alarm batching switches from calendar-object references to calendar.id strings for add/modify suppression, and alarm removal checks the located window for a removeWidgetFor property before calling it. This presence check is narrower than full dialog readiness. The actual dialog method updates selection when removing the selected widget; no live focus or accessibility result is claimed.",
        "The original shared alarm test captures a querySelectorAll result once, then waits on that saved result’s length. A later accepted version queries inside each poll and asserts the returned count. The original gets a nonempty message added to its one-widget assertion; runTestAlarms already takes no parameters and all six protocol caller arguments are removed. Existing fixed 500 ms and 2,000 ms waits remain separate timing limits.",
        "The moved unit alarm setup retains two ok calls without messages. Touched Calendar manager observer context also has equal calls without messages, and free/busy touched contexts retain similar gaps. Newly improved browser alarm messages do not establish that all affected test diagnostics are complete. No missing should-only alternative is reported as a defect.",
        "getWeekTitle retains a string JSDoc/IDL description, but the direct singleton JS method returns Math.ceil-derived weekNumber. Actual module consumers use it as a DOM attribute or localization argument. This is a scoped direct-result/documentation mismatch, not a demonstrated rendering failure or an invented general naming rule.",
        "The exact side-effect import is present in the owned commit, but its adjacent eslint exception still says no-unused-vars; accepted later source uses import/no-unassigned-import as the review replacement requested. Class conversion, Sunday capitalization, provider/observer QueryInterface additions, and removal of unused alarm-helper caller arguments are source-confirmed. The review’s alarm-plan reversal is preserved separately from an unproven runtime mechanism.",
        "Remaining manager and timezone component registrations still name their exports as constructors, while those exports are singleton values. This exact metadata/value-shape difference is retained as a bounded integration question; the upstream component-factory implementation and a native lookup result were not independently verified. No factory failure is asserted.",
        "Complete original Parent primary 2022873 and C own D295631 scopes are inherited, including all 13 actual inline bodies and the single literal replacement. B checked the needed bodies for adoption. The request to explain eager timezone initialization is answered by the reason comment and side-effect import; the owned no-unused-vars exception differs from the requested and accepted-later import/no-unassigned-import exception. Do not collapse those phases.",
        "The reviewer rejects accepting two alarms. The author first proposes a separate timing fix, then explicitly revises that plan: this patch needs a small fix and the rest goes to 2038199/D301047. The original retains a one-alarm assertion, calendar-ID batching and monitor capability guards; no single mechanism or successful test run is inferred from that discussion. The unused helper parameter is actually removed from all six callers even though the thread remains Not Done.",
        "Class conversion, the observer/provider interface requests and Sunday capitalization have actual owned/current support. Generic comma comments have no separately verified target-code span here, so no particular comma restoration is invented. Full historical re-review, application/rebase and ongoing/failed-build landing are team context, not fresh lint/build results."
